title: Veterans Who Fought for Our Freedom May Finally Get Medical Cannabis

content_html_sanitized:
The excellent website, MarijuanaMoment.net, has a story,

The VA Is Hiring A Contractor To Help Explain Medical Marijuana’s Benefits And Risks For Military Veterans.

 

Really? Really!

 

“The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is looking for contractors to analyze and explain scientific evidence on medical marijuana to clinicians and the general public as part of VA’s Systematically Testing the Evidence of Marijuana (STEM) project.

The work aims to evaluate and allow VA to more clearly communicate cannabis’s potential benefits for conditions like PTSD as well as potential risks around cannabis use disorder and consumption during pregnancy.”

The dateline on the story was actually May 6, so my apologies for being late, but when it comes to marijuana and veterans, what’s a few weeks or decades, here and there?

Veterans and marijuana first met over fifty years ago when the Vietnam War met the Drug War, and they were on the losing side in both.

At first, it looked like the anti war “potheads” and the Veterans were on opposite sides, but it soon became obvious that when veterans got home, they had no choice.

In 1972, at NORML’s First People’s Pot Conference, I had the memorable opportunity to smoke some extraordinary pot (as we generally called it then) that had been grown in Arkansas by an Air Force veteran, who had been a pilot for a famous general. He had become very cynical about both wars. The only thing he was certain about was that Americans would suffer and die. And he loved the plant about which we still knew very little. But the Drug Warriors knew enough. See Richard Nixon Privately Admitted Marijuana Was 'Not Particularly Dangerous' “The recordings demonstrate yet again that drug warriors always knew marijuana wasn't that bad—they just didn't care.”

It wasn’t long before disabled veterans discovered that cannabis could help them with chronic pain from their injuries and PTSD from the trauma of war. But it wasn’t just Nixon who did not care. The US Government didn’t care. See Support Our Troops Unless It Interferes with the Drug War Then Let Them Suffer and Die?? Analysis by Richard Cowan

For many years Veterans could be arrested for using medical marijuana and lose their veterans benefits. And I knew some who were, and I will be writing about them soon. Eventually, some state laws changed, and even though the VA doctors still cannot prescribe medical cannabis, they are at least allowed to discuss it with their patients. Unfortunately, as the story about the VA hiring consultants demonstrates, most doctors really don’t know that much about it.

See VA and Marijuana – What Veterans need to know.

Although 39 states in the U.S. have approved the use of marijuana for medical and/or recreational use, federal law still classifies marijuana as a “Schedule One Controlled Substance.” Even though DEA FINALLY CONFIRMS THE EXISTENCE OF SUFFICIENT GROUNDS TO REMOVE MARIJUANA FROM HARD DRUGS SCHEDULE OF CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES In 1998! But 27 years later, it is still illegal in the eyes of the federal government, even though Marijuana in Veterans’ Medical Treatment: Medical cannabis as an alternative to opioids for veterans

Finally, Federal Study Finds Cannabis Beneficial for PTSD Treatment. Results of a study released in march revealed improvements among PTSD patients receiving cannabis doses with higher levels of THC

Now think about that for a moment. A veteran who has PTSD as a result of fighting for his country, the land of the free, and all that good stuff, needs to use a plant that will help him, but his government would put him in jail for it. The ultimate example of adding insult to injury.
